# PCB Parts MCP Server

> MCP server for electronic component data: a searchable daily snapshot of JLCPCB's in-stock catalog (630K+ parts with stock >= 10), live stock and prices from JLCPCB, Mouser and DigiKey, EasyEDA pinouts and footprints, SamacSys KiCad files, reference board schematics, sensor lookup and PCB design rules.

- Endpoint: `https://pcbparts.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless)
- Auth: none
- Rate limit: 100 requests a minute per IP
- Health: `https://pcbparts.dev/health`
- Source: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp

## Setup

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add -s user --transport http pcbparts https://pcbparts.dev/mcp
```

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`); VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`) uses the key `"servers"` instead of `"mcpServers"`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pcbparts": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Clients that only run local commands (Copilot for Xcode): `{"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"]}`.

## Which tool

- Find parts: `jlc_search`. Confirm stock before ordering, or find parts with stock under 10: `jlc_stock_check`.
- Recorded low-stock observations for one LCSC code: `jlc_stock_history`; missing scrape records are not confirmed stockouts.
- One part's live details: `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)`. A manufacturer part number to JLCPCB parts: `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)`.
- Replacement for a part: get its LCSC code (from `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)` if needed), then `jlc_find_alternatives(lcsc=...)`.
- Mouser or DigiKey data: `mouser_get_part`, `digikey_get_part`, only when the user wants that distributor.
- Pins and footprint pads: `jlc_get_pinout`. KiCad files: `cse_get_kicad` (slow).
- How real boards wire an IC: `board_search(component=...)`, then `board_get(slug, focus=IC)`.
- Choosing a sensor: `sensor_recommend`. Design guidance: `get_design_rules`.

## Tools

Optional filters and identity arguments default to null unless stated otherwise. Result limits are integers clamped to each tool's range. `library_type` accepts `basic`, `preferred`, `no_fee` (basic or preferred), `extended`, `all`; ignores case and surrounding whitespace; accepts `no-fee`. `packages` and `manufacturers` accept arrays, JSON-array strings or one literal string, never comma-split (max 50 items each).

### jlc_search

Searches the daily snapshot (stock >= 10). Stock is as of `data_as_of`; the 1-piece price is refreshed weekly, as of `prices_as_of` (a part new since then has its first scraped price).

- Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters; plain words, e.g. "100nF 25V X7R 0402"), `subcategory_name` or `subcategory_id`, `spec_filters`, `package` or `packages` (OR, max 50), `manufacturer`, `min_stock` (default 10, clamped to at least 0), `library_type`, `prefer_no_fee` (default true: basic and preferred first), `pcba_type` ("economic" or "standard_only"), `sort_by` ("stock" by default, "price" or "spec"), `sort_spec`, `sort_order`, `limit` (default 20, clamped to 1-100), `offset` (default 0, clamped to 0-10000), `strict` (default false), `match_all_terms` (default true), `facets` (default false).
- `spec_filters`: array or JSON-array string, up to 50 of `{"name", "op", "value"}`, e.g. `[{"name": "Vgs(th)", "op": "<", "value": "2V"}]`; values accept text or numbers. Operators `=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` (`=>` normalizes to `>=`); `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` work only on numeric specs. Several `=` filters on one spec match any of the values (OR), except `Supply Voltage` and `Vin`, where a part must cover all of them (AND). Names ignore case. Unitless values use base units (V, A, ohms, F, H, Hz, W, mm, bytes). `jlc_search_help(subcategory=...)` lists a subcategory's specs, which are numeric, and which sort.
- Battery holders: a query naming a battery, cell, coin cell or button cell holder searches all holder subcategories. Sizes AA (No. 5, 14500), AAA (No. 7, 10440), C (No. 2), D (No. 1) and coin or button cell match the part's text and show as `Battery Size` in `filters_applied.spec_filters`; two sizes mean either. Other sizes (18650) are plain search words.
- Short spec names: `Vgs(th)`, `Vds`, `Id`, `Rds(on)`, `Vr`, `If`, `Vf`, `Vceo`, `Ic`, `Vout`, `Iout`, `Quiescent Current` (`Iq`), `Supply Voltage`, `Isolation Voltage`, `Capacitance`, `Resistance`, `Inductance`, `Voltage`, `Tolerance`, `Power`, `DCR`, `Isat`, `Frequency`, `Load Capacitance`, `Junction Capacitance`, `Reverse Stand-Off Voltage (Vrwm)`, `Operating Temperature` (°C).
- Sorting by a spec: `sort_spec` (e.g. "RDS(on)@4.5V", "Dropout@500mA", "Vf@1A", "Iq", "Isat") with `sort_order` "asc" (default) or "desc". A query can supply the spec instead ("lowest Iq LDO"); `sort_order` with neither, or `sort_by="spec"` without `sort_spec`, is an error. Parts that don't list the spec come last. Rows add `sort_value` (the figure sorted on); `sort` says what was compared, and `sort.note` says when figures at different test conditions were compared as listed.
- Reply: `results`, `total` (every match before pagination), `page_info` (`limit`, `offset`, `returned`), `library_type_counts`, `no_fee_available`; part-number searches add `mpn_matches` counts. Part rows: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price`, `library_type`, `preferred`, `category`, `subcategory`, `subcategory_id`, `mounting_type`, `specs`, `data_source`; optional `description` when specs are absent, and annotations below or from reviewed evidence. `filters_applied` lists every filter that ran; `parsed` what the query text gave. `relaxed` names query words, a query-only library preference or a part type left out to get results; `relaxed.dropped_filters` lists parsed spec filters dropped when a part number was retried, so those results don't meet them. `parsed.adjusted_filters` lists specs moved or left out (including a package that fell back to its bare family); `ignored_filters` filters not applied or rarely listed. `unlisted` counts parts a range filter left out only because they list no value. `hint` on an empty reply suggests a next step. `counts_complete=false` means the counts are partial. `valid_values` lists accepted inputs on an error.
- `facets=true` adds manufacturer, package and library_type counts over the full final effective search, independent of pagination. Every active filter applies, including the facet's own field. `facets` has `scope="filtered_snapshot"`, `matched_total`, `complete`, `status` ("complete", "incomplete", "unavailable") and `elapsed_ms`. Each field has up to 15 `buckets` (`value`, `count`), sorted by count descending then value, plus `omitted_buckets` and `omitted_count`. Library values are basic/preferred/extended; no_fee means basic plus preferred, not a separate bucket. Exact counts appear only with complete status; otherwise matched_total is null and buckets are absent. Facets use a private read connection with their own about 200 ms / 2,000,000 SQLite VM step / 5,000 Python-candidate budget; exhaustion preserves the search results.
- Accepted spellings: `pcba_type` ignores case, spaces and hyphens and accepts "standard" (= standard_only) and "economic_and_standard" (= economic); `sort_order` accepts ascending/lowest and descending/highest; `sort_by` ignores case.
- LDO dropout at a load: `{"name": "Dropout", "op": "<=", "value": "0.3V@500mA"}` uses each part's listed dropout at or above that load, or scales a lower test current's figure up linearly; parts rated only below the load are left out. Rows add `dropout_at_load` saying which figure was used.
- USB-PD: controller, sink, source or trigger wording selects PD controllers over USB-C connectors. Sink/trigger and source rank listed receiver/supply controllers first, and a sink voltage ranks matching negotiated Output Voltage within the role; parts missing those attributes stay in the results unless `strict=true`. Strict sink-and-source requirements are reported as unsupported.
- When the search shortens a part number (`LM1117-3.3` searches `LM1117`), `mpn_match` on each result is `full`, `same_suffix` or `family`, in that order.
- MOSFET queries with a gate drive add `rds_on_at_drive`: the RDS(on) listed at or below that drive, or null when none is listed there. Null parts stay in the results.
- `pcba_type="standard_only"` on a part means one such part moves the whole order to Standard assembly. `no_datasheet=true` means JLCPCB lists no datasheet; `no_datasheet_note` clarifies that LCSC or the manufacturer may have one.

### jlc_stock_check

Live JLCPCB search over the whole catalog (7M+ parts). Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters), `category_name`/`category_id`, `subcategory_name`/`subcategory_id`, `package`/`packages`, `manufacturer`/`manufacturers`, `library_type`, `min_stock` (default 10, clamped to at least 0; 0 includes out-of-stock), `sort_by` ("quantity" default, "price"), `page` (default 1, clamped to at least 1), `limit` (default 20, clamped to 1-100). JLCPCB matches whole part numbers and their starts, not text inside them. One LCSC code as `query` returns that part only, with its price tiers.

Reply: `results`, `page`, `per_page`, `total`, `total_pages`, `has_more`. Results use the JLC part-row fields above with live `data_source`; a single-code lookup also includes `prices` (`qty`, `price`) where listed. `hint` appears when an LCSC code matches nothing (with the min_stock and filters applied) and when a part-number fragment matches no part number from its start but is inside in-stock ones ("2812" names WS2812B).

### jlc_stock_history

Recorded events for one `lcsc` C-code: C followed by 1-12 digits (case and surrounding spaces ignored). Event `type` is `change`, `new`, `gone`, `reappear` or `type_change`. `days` defaults to 180, integer 1-366, ending on the newest recorded date rather than today. At most 100 events, newest first; `more_events=true` means older events in that window were omitted.

Reply: `lcsc`, `window` (`start`, `end`, `history_start`, `history_end`, inclusive ISO dates), `events` (`date`, `type`, `stock_after`, `note`, optional `stock_before`), `more_events`, `what_is_recorded` (plain-language recording limits), `current_stock` (snapshot quantity, null if unlisted), `current_stock_as_of` (snapshot time, possibly null). An empty history DB has null window dates. Unknown codes and parts without events return `events: []` normally. A missing/unreadable history DB returns an error.

Changes are recorded only when resulting stock is <=1,000 and absolute change exceeds 10 at 0-100, 25 at 101-500 or 100 at 501-1,000. An empty history does not establish stable stock: stock above 1,000 and small changes are not tracked. New records require 0 < stock <=1,000; reappear from a listed zero and library-type changes are independent of this cap. `gone` has `stock_after: null`: it means missing from a scrape, possibly delisted, below its 10-unit floor or a scrape gap, never a confirmed zero or ongoing stockout. A scrape gap that empties whole subcategories at once is not recorded as gone: those parts keep their previous stock for up to two days (the past gap days were corrected the same way). Notes label remaining disappearances on those gap dates (2026-03-03, 03-16, 03-18, 05-15) and returns within two days as `suspect_scrape`. Other dates are not certified complete; 2026-08-07 is missing. Returns above 1,000 may be unrecorded. Past events have no before-values; `stock_before` appears only when actually recorded from the previous snapshot. Current stock is separate snapshot data, not live. No predictions or availability percentages.

### jlc_get_part

- `lcsc` (e.g. "C82899"): live details, cached up to an hour.
- `mpn` (e.g. "LM358P", max 100 characters): searches the daily snapshot (stock >= 10) and returns `{mpn, results, total}`; call `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` on a result for live stock and full details. It also finds other dash and space spellings, the same maker's packing codes and BOM text with notes ("TL074 OP AMP"), and never a different grade. Inexact matches add `match` (`separators`, `packing`, `alias`, `alternative`, `lcsc`, `related`) and `matched_mpn`; `related` results can be other part types.

Provide `lcsc` or `mpn`; a nonempty `lcsc` wins when both are supplied.

Snapshot part rows carry `data_source` (`kind`, `provider`, `observed_at`, plus `specs_provider` "LCSC" when LCSC supplied the specs); live lookup observations keep their time through caching. MPN hits include `data_as_of` and `prices_as_of`; misses identify snapshot scope, `availability: unknown_outside_snapshot`, and an optional unexecuted live-check `next_call`.

Reply fields: `prices` (quantity tiers), `datasheet_pdf` (a stable link to the PDF), `datasheet` (LCSC's viewer page, null when none), `maker_datasheet` (the manufacturer's link, where listed), `datasheet_note`, `specs`, `specs_note` (what the listing leaves out for the part type), `spec_evidence` (where reviewed: manufacturer values, conditions, document, printed page, source URL, review date), `spec_discrepancies` (known catalog/document conflicts; catalog specs and numeric filtering/sorting are preserved), `pcba_type`, `lcsc_url`, `min_order`, `reel_qty`, `has_easyeda_footprint` (null = unknown, false = none), `easyeda_symbol_uuid`, `easyeda_footprint_uuid`. No lifecycle status: use `mouser_get_part` or `digikey_get_part`.

Savings use a rounded legacy $3 Economic loading-fee estimate, labelled with `is_estimate` and `assembly_service_assumption`; confirm current quotes. Standard service differs.

### jlc_get_pinout

`lcsc` or `uuid` (EasyEDA symbol; a nonempty `lcsc` wins), `footprint` (default false; needs `lcsc`). Reply: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package` (these four may be null with UUID-only lookup), `pin_count`, `pins`, `easyeda_symbol_uuid`. Pin numbers and names exactly as the EasyEDA symbol has them; numbers match the EasyEDA footprint's pads. `electrical` appears only where the symbol sets it. `unverified` (the string "Symbol not verified by LCSC") is present when LCSC hasn't verified the symbol. `note`: the pins are named only by number, or a diode/LED-type part whose numbering varies between sources (connect it by pin name). `footprint=true` adds `footprint` with name, `source_link`, `pad_count`, `numbered_pads`, `pitch`, `pad_sizes` and `pads` (number, x, y in mm from the origin with y down, shape, size, layer, hole, slot_length); if the footprint can't be fetched, the pins still come back with `footprint_error`.

Empty `jlc_search` responses can include `why_empty`: tested library/package/stock changes, retained constraints, counts with exact/at_least relation, executable next calls where representable, and `diagnostics_complete`, plus `status` when the checks didn't finish: "budget_exhausted_or_busy" (out of time or the snapshot was busy) or "diagnostic_failed". Only the stock>=10 snapshot is checked. Diagnostics are bounded to three queries/200 ms; incomplete work is explicit and original results remain empty. Negative Vout preserves polarity; impedance@frequency compares that frequency; part-number exclusions are reported as unsupported.

### jlc_find_alternatives

`lcsc` (required LCSC code), `library_type`, `same_package` (default false), `has_easyeda_footprint` (true/false filter, default null: no filter), `min_stock` (default 10, clamped to at least 0), `limit` (per list, default 10, clamped to 1-50), `board_quantity` and `placements_per_board` (default 1, each a positive integer, for `comparison.savings`).

- `summary.found` counts `alternatives`: parts whose primary value and required specs match (connector series and contacts, transistor polarity, regulator output and listed input range) and whose readable ratings are the same or better. Ranked basic/preferred first.
- Ratings that are missing or unreadable don't disqualify a part: they're listed in `specs_unparseable`. `unchecked_requirements` lists what wasn't checked; pinout and external circuit always need checking. A regulator's single input rating checks only the maximum.
- `unverified_alternatives` miss a required match or lack comparable rating conditions: compare by hand. Inductor Isat needs comparable inductance-drop criteria and rating bases; thermal current needs matching thermal conditions and bases; DCR needs comparable published bases. Multi-diode current comparisons need loading/thermal evidence. These candidates do not drive the recommended savings comparison.
- `has_easyeda_footprint` checks at most `min(2 * limit, 15)` candidates after library/package eligibility; unknown availability is excluded for both true and false. Extended fallback examples use only the remaining check budget when no verified no-fee result was found. `summary.footprint_filter` reports either cap and lookup failures.
- `summary.stages`: `retrieval` counts per source (`retrieved`, `limit`, `hit_limit`, `error`: null or "retrieval_failed"; database also `scanned`, `scan_limit`, `scan_hit_limit`); `primary` and `specs` counts (`passed`, `failed`, `unknown`); `eligibility.library/package` passed/failed; `footprints` checked/compatible/incompatible/unknown, `not_checked_cap`, `eligible_checked`, `fallback_checked`; `output` per-list truncation counts and `limit_per_list`. Retrieval counts precede deduplication and source-specific filtering; subsequent stages describe the merged candidates. Unknown spec counts include unreadable ratings and do not change verified/manual classification. Bounds reached do not prove more matches exist; retrieval errors remain visible alongside any usable results.
- Part types without rules return `similar_parts`. RF parts are ordered by `frequency_coverage` of the original's range. Modules and others list the same package and part family first, marked `likely_drop_in` (pinout unchecked).
- Lifecycle (NRND) isn't checked.
- Reply: `original`, `search_criteria`, `summary`; part types with rules add `alternatives`, `unverified_alternatives`, `comparison` (`original`, `recommended`, `savings`) and `confidence` (`level` high/medium/low, `reason`, `unchecked_requirements`); others add `similar_parts` and `manual_comparison`. Rows add `score`, `score_breakdown`, `specs_verified`, `specs_unparseable`, `unchecked_requirements`, and where they apply `verification_status`, `unverified_requirements`, `moq_warning`, `package_warning`.

### jlc_search_help

No arguments: all categories. `category` (name string or integer ID): its subcategories. `subcategory` (name string or integer ID, takes precedence over category): its filterable specs with type and example values, marked `sort_spec` where sortable.

Replies: no arguments `{categories: [{id, name, count, subcategory_count}]}`; category `{category_id, category_name, subcategories: [{id, name, count}]}`; subcategory `{subcategory_id, subcategory_name, category_name, sample_size, attributes}`, each attribute `{name, alias, type, count, example_values, values, min, max, total_unique, sort_spec}` where present. Attributes are sampled from up to 1,000 parts of the subcategory; `values` holds at most 50, and `total_unique` appears when there are more. An unknown category returns `error` and `hint`.

### mouser_get_part

`part_number` (required, max 500 characters total): a Mouser PN or MPN (3-40 characters each), or up to 10 joined by "|" ("595-LM358P|NE555P"), one request per call. Matching is loose and returns at most 50 results: use full part numbers when batching and match results by `mfr_part_number`. Check `manufacturer`: a number can match another maker's part. `lifecycle` is Mouser's status where it gives one, else null.

Reply: `{results, total}`, optional `not_found` listing unmatched inputs. Each result: `source`, `part_number`, `mfr_part_number`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `category`, `stock`, `price`, `price_breaks` (`qty`, `price`, `currency`), `datasheet_url`, `product_url`, `rohs`, `lifecycle`, `parameters`, `min_qty`, `currency`, `unit_weight_g`.

### digikey_get_part

`product_number` (required, max 500 characters): one DigiKey PN or full MPN per call (one keyword search per lookup; a partial number can find nothing and still uses a request; a miss includes a `hint` suggesting a DigiKey PN unless the input already ends in `-ND`). `part_number`, `price`, `price_breaks` and `min_qty` are one packaging's (the PN given, else the smallest order); `packaging` names it and `other_packaging` lists the rest. `lifecycle` is DigiKey's product status.

Reply: `{results, total}`. A number several makers use returns each maker's listing, most stock first. Each result has the shared Mouser fields above except `unit_weight_g`; its `price_breaks` contain only `qty` and `price`, using the result's `currency`. Optional `packaging`, `other_packaging` (`part_number`, `packaging`, `min_qty`, `price`), and `reel_fee`/`marketplace` on the result or other packaging.

### cse_search, cse_get_kicad

SamacSys ComponentSearchEngine; slow: a search takes about 15 s, longer when busy; answers are cached. No overall tool deadline. Search HTTP requests use `CSE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (default 45 s per request phase); a non-Success API status is retried once after 3 s. Model downloads use a fixed 30 s timeout per request phase.

- `cse_search`: required `query` (max 500 characters), `limit` (default 5, clamped to 1-10); no credentials needed. Reply: `{results, total}`. Each result: `source`, `mfr_part_number`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `datasheet_url`, `has_model` (generic ECAD availability), `has_3d`, `model_quality`, `cse_part_id`, `pin_count`, `image_url`. Individual KiCad/Eagle/Altium formats are not confirmed.
- `cse_get_kicad`: `query` (string, max 500 characters) or `part_id` (integer), both default null; at least one needed, a nonzero `part_id` wins. Query selection takes the first search result with `has_model` and `cse_part_id`, with no separate best-match scoring. Requires `CSEARCH_USER` and `CSEARCH_PASS`. Reply: `part_id`, search metadata fields above when resolved by query, `kicad_symbol` (`.kicad_sym` text), `kicad_footprint` (`.kicad_mod` text); either file may be null. Archives over 50 MiB are rejected; files over 10 MiB are skipped.

### board_search, board_get

`board_search`: `component` (IC name, max 200 characters; adds a cross-board `consensus` when 2+ boards match), `query` (max 500 characters; function, e.g. "motor driver"), `tag` (one string, list or JSON-array string, AND semantics; ignores case/surrounding whitespace, `usb-c` aliases `usb`; lists discard nonstrings/items over 200 characters after normalization, then keep at most 10), `org` (max 200 characters), `layers`, `limit` (default 10, clamped to 1-50). Unknown tags return `valid_values`. Consensus `pct` divides by `consensus.board_count`.

Search reply: `{total, results}`; each result has `slug`, `name`, `org`, `org_display`, `source`, `source_url`, `format`, `description`, `key_coverage`, `tags`, `key_ics`, `layers`, `width_mm`, `height_mm`, `component_count`, `ic_count`, plus `matched_by` when a filter explains the match. Tag-only browsing of one tag may add `tag_consensus`; empty results may add `hint`. A `query` with no searchable words (only stop words such as board, design and pcb, or single characters; quotes and OR are not operators) browses the catalog, keeping the other filters, and the reply's `note` says so.

`board_get`: required `slug` (1-200 characters), `focus` (max 200 characters; IC name, ref like "J1", or value words like "USB-C": returns that part's pin-by-pin neighborhood), `include_bom` (default false; adds plain passives), `include_nets` (default false; full netlist, can be 100 KB+).

Detail reply: board identity/metadata fields above (without `matched_by`), plus `min_trace`, `min_clearance`, `min_drill`, `min_via`, `net_count`. Without focus: `components`, `neighborhoods` summaries, `passives_omitted` when any plain passives were hidden. Components carry `ref`, `value`, `footprint` and available descriptions/ratings/annotations, plus the design files' `mpn`, `manufacturer`, `lcsc`, `mouser`, `digikey` where listed. With focus: `focus` (`ref`, `value`, `pins`), `focus_match_type` (ref/exact/partial), optional `consensus` and `focus_alternatives`. `power_pins` and `pin_nets` appear on focus only when present; `pins_in_nets` counts the named pins in nets; `pin_count` and `nc_pins` appear where source pin information exists (`{}` means all connected). A focus miss adds `focus_error`, `available_ics` and, when present, `available_refs`. `include_nets=true` adds `nets`, `positions`, `copper_pours`. Unknown slug errors may add `did_you_mean`.

### sensor_recommend

`query` (max 500 characters), `measure` (one string, list or JSON-array string of up to 20), `type`, `protocol`, `platform` ("arduino", "esphome", "micropython", "circuitpython", "tasmota", "zephyr", "raspberry_pi"), `limit` (default 15, clamped to 1-100). Unknown measure, protocol and platform values return `valid_values`; an unknown type returns no matches. Ordering: exact normalized query-ID/alias matches first, then `platform_count` descending, then name ascending. Not for buying: use `jlc_search`.

Measures in a list all must match. `imu` expands to acceleration/gyroscope/magnetic_field with OR for a scalar or singleton list; in a multi-item list all expanded measures are required. Measure aliases include heart rate/blood oxygen→biometric, barometric→pressure, lux→light, dust→particulate and compass→magnetic_field. Protocols: i2c/i3c/spi/uart/analog/pwm/gpio/one_wire/rs485/rs232/can/i2s/usb/ble/hdq/ssi (accepted values come from the catalog; an unknown one returns `valid_values`); `gpio` includes gpio/analog/pwm/one_wire, `digital` includes gpio/pwm/one_wire, `1-wire`/`one-wire` alias one_wire. Measure/protocol/platform/type filters ignore case and surrounding whitespace.

Reply: `{total, results}`, plus `note` when `query` has no searchable words (stop words, single letters, symbols), which leaves only the filters; each result has `id`, `name`, `manufacturer`, `type`, `voltage`, `datasheet_url`, `platform_count`, `description`, `source_tier`, `measures`, `protocols`, `platforms`, `urls`, plus optional evidence fields below.

`voltage` is the supply in volts, "min-max" or a single value. Parts sold in separate supply versions or with separate supply modes list each, e.g. "3.0-3.6 or 4.5-5.5" (pick the version you order); a record covering several chips gives the range all of them support. Null when the part has no supply of its own (passive elements, probes, heated gas cells) or no maker source states one. A `capability_note` covers other rails (LED, VDDIO, mains) and a narrower supply that full specifications need (DS1821: accuracy and 1-Wire timing at 3.6-5.5V).

Sensor capability notes: calculated CO2 (CCS811, ENS160, ENS161, SGP30, iAQ-Core, APC1, SM300D2) is under `eco2`, not `co2`; BME680 and BME688 note that Bosch's BSEC library calculates IAQ and CO2 equivalent on the host. `capability_note` says what such a part really outputs. CCS811, ENS160 and SGP30 also have `compensation_inputs` and operating/stress `voltage_evidence`; compensation inputs are not selectable direct measurements. For ENS160, ENS161 and the ENS16x library the listed voltage is VDD (1.71-1.98V); VDDIO is separate (1.71-3.6V). Descriptions prefer device/integration sources over breakout marketing.

### get_design_rules

`topic` (default `""`; non-index topics truncated to 500 characters): empty or index (`INDEX.md`) returns `INDEX.md`, which lists every file. Exact normalized keys (`power/ldo`), aliases (`type-c`, `lipo`, `ws2812`, `debounce`, `nordic`, `fiducial`) and token-boundary category/filename matching select files; MCU family prefixes such as `stm32g0` also match. Otherwise a scored text fallback selects the files discussing the topic most.

Reply: `{content, matched_files, topic}`, with `note` on text-fallback matches. Up to three matching files return full content; more than three return a key list asking for a narrower topic. No matches returns the index with an explanation and empty `matched_files`.

## How jlc_search reads a query

- Units: `u`/`µ`/`μ` mean micro, `4u7` is 4.7uF (4.7uH for inductors), `6V3` is 6.3V. `10M`/`10Meg` are megaohms, `10m` milliohms. A value has at most 4 significant digits before a unit letter (`1000R`, `4R75`); a longer run such as `9774025151R` is searched as a part number. A part number, including one that starts with 7+ digits (`61300211121`, `10118194-0001LF`), is searched on its own; other words in the query are listed in `parsed.detected.not_searched` (`strict=true` keeps them). Package `1005` is `0402`.
- A value goes to the spec the part type lists: `5V relay` is the coil voltage, `3.3V LDO` the output, `12V buck` an output range covering 12V, `3.3V level shifter` a supply range covering it, `24V input 3.3V output` both sides of a regulator. A current under 1mA in an LDO/DC-DC query is the quiescent current. A resistance with an ohm unit on MOSFETs, load switches or inductors is a maximum RDS(on) or DCR. If the part type doesn't list the spec, the value is left out and `parsed.adjusted_filters` says so.
- In a MOSFET query, a voltage next to `logic level`, `GPIO` or `MCU` (up to 5V) or `gate`/`Vgs` (up to 20V) is the gate drive; parts with RDS(on) listed at or below it rank first.
- Comparisons in the text keep their operator: `Iq < 10uA`, `Vf < 0.3V`. A sign before a bare value applies to the main rating (`10uF capacitor < 25V`).
- Ranges (supply/output voltage, operating temperature): `=` matches a range that includes the value, `>=` one that reaches it, `<=` one that goes down to it. `-40°C` in a query means rated down to -40°C, `105C` up to 105°C.
- Connectors filter on pin count and pitch where the connector type lists them (`JST PH 2 pin`); `qwiic`/`STEMMA QT` mean 4-pin 1.0mm JST SH, `Grove` 4-pin 2.0mm. A query searches one pitch: a second mm length is left out (`parsed.detected.not_searched`) unless named. Headers take named lengths: `insulation height 5mm` (also body/plastic height), `mating pin length`, `tail length`, with `at least`, `under`, `>` etc.; `Insulation Height`, `Length of Mating Pin` and `Length of End Connection Pin` are numeric, so `spec_filters` can use `>`, `<` and ranges on them.
- Packages include their other spellings: `SOT-23` includes `SOT-23-3`, `0603` includes `1608`, a bare `QFN-32` matches VQFN/WQFN/UQFN of any body. `QFN-24-EP(4x4)` keeps the body and exposed pad; if no catalog package has that body, the bare family is matched and `parsed.adjusted_filters` says so (`strict=true` doesn't fall back).
- `basic`, `preferred` and `no fee` in the query set the library filter; `cheapest` sorts by price; `lowest Iq`, `highest Isat`, `most flash` sort by that spec. Arguments win over query words; `library_type="all"` overrides a library word.
- Query words that match nothing together with the rest are left out and named in `relaxed`. With `subcategory_name` or `spec_filters` given, they aren't left out: the reply is empty and `hint` names them. `strict=true` turns off every relaxation and returns an error for unsupported constraints.
- Spec figures are JLCPCB's listings; check datasheets before choosing.

## Library types

| Type | Economic loading fee | Meaning |
|------|--------------|---------|
| `basic` | none | JLCPCB's standard library |
| `preferred` | none | Recommended parts with good availability |
| `extended` | Fee per unique type; calculator uses a rounded $3 estimate | Everything else |
| `no_fee` | none | Filter for basic and preferred together |
| `all` | | No library filter |

## Quotas

The Mouser and DigiKey daily limits are shared by everyone on pcbparts.dev (DigiKey's resets at 00:00 UTC), with at most 25 requests a minute for Mouser and 100 for DigiKey. Batch Mouser lookups, look up one DigiKey part at a time, and don't retry a quota error. Self-hosting with your own keys gives your own limits: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp#self-hosting
